extraction.name: XTREME-S
extraction.description: A benchmark for evaluating universal cross-lingual speech representations across 102 languages and four task families: speech recognition, classification, speech-to-text translation, and retrieval. It includes seven downstream tasks and a new multilingual evaluation dataset called Fleurs.
extraction.creator: Alexis Conneau, Ankur Bapna, Yu Zhang, Min Ma, Patrick von Platen, Anton Lozhkov, Colin Cherry, Ye Jia, Clara Rivera, Mihir Kale, Daan Van Esch, Vera Axelrod, Simran Khanuja, Jonathan H. Clark, Orhan Firat, Michael Auli, Sebastian Ruder, Jason Riesa, Melvin Johnson

extraction.rai:dataCollection: The section describes evaluation on existing speech datasets and notes that the train/dev/test sets of Fleurs are used for speech retrieval; it also mentions multilingual training built from Minds- and supervision provided by CoVoST-2.
extraction.rai:dataCollectionRawData: Existing speech datasets including Fleurs, MLS, VoxPopuli, CoVoST-2, and Minds-.
extraction.rai:dataBiases: The benchmark is designed around a diverse and representative set of tasks and languages, but it still reflects the available multilingual speech data and focuses on 102 languages spanning more than 10 language families.
extraction.rai:dataLimitations: The paper notes that prior studies evaluated on a small and often disparate set of languages, which makes comparisons difficult and hinders assessment of generalization; XTREME-S is introduced to address this evaluation limitation.
extraction.rai:dataSocialImpact: The dataset/benchmark is intended to improve speech technology for under-represented languages, giving speakers an equal voice on the Internet and helping make their content and culture known outside their language cluster.
extraction.rai:dataUseCases: Used as a multilingual speech evaluation benchmark for cross-lingual transfer learning and learned speech representations; it covers recognition, translation, classification, and retrieval tasks, and includes a general-purpose evaluation dataset (Fleurs) across 102 languages.
